results.title: Hetzner Price Increase 2026: What Changed and What to Do
results.author: Petr Hess
highlights:
We checked the published 2026 price history against the live Hetzner Cloud API on 5 November 2026 (all eight CX and CAX prices match the June list) and put measured output next to it: the CX33 now costs 8.49 euro net and delivered 13.5 tokens/s on Llama 3.2 3B and 31.93 n8n executions/s on our server.

The Hetzner price increase 2026 came in two cloud rounds: 1 April 2026 and 15 June 2026. Together they took the cheapest x86 server, the CX23, from 2.99 euro to 5.49 euro net per month, an 83.6 % rise, and the x86 CPX and CCX lines rose far more in June. We checked those numbers against the Hetzner Cloud API on 5 November 2026, and all eight CX and CAX prices match the June list.

...

## What changed in 2026, with dates

- Early February 2026: one-time setup fees for dedicated servers went up, per heise.
- 1 April 2026: a broad price rise across Hetzner's products, cloud included. heise reported on 23 February 2026 that both new orders and existing products were affected and that Hetzner made no exceptions for long-term contracts. Hetzner cited sharply higher operating costs and much higher procurement costs for new hardware, naming RAM and NVMe SSD prices.
- 15 June 2026, 8:00 CEST: a second cloud and dedicated round. Hetzner's cloud changelog entry of 28 May 2026 says "updated pricing for cloud servers will apply to new orders and rescales". Existing servers keep their price unless you rescale them. heise reported average rises of about 158 % for US data centres, 99 % for Germany and just under 78 % for Singapore, with the US CPX41 going from 38.99 to 120.49 euro per month.
- 26 June 2026: Hetzner posted a status notice, "Limited availability of cloud instances", restricting new servers for new customers and for some existing customers chosen at random, citing "the limited availability of required hardware components".
- 7 July and 6 October 2026: new small CPX types arrived in the EU, the CPX12 (1 vCPU, 2 GB) and the CPX02 (1 vCPU, 1 GB), per the same changelog.

...

results.title: Hetzner GPU Servers Compared: Prices, VRAM | WZ-IT
results.author: Timo Wevelsiep
highlights:
Hetzner rebuilt its GPU range in autumn 2026: the GEX45 arrived on 1 September, the GEX63 on 6 October, and the GEX44 can no longer be ordered. Many comparisons online therefore list models and prices that no longer apply.

This article puts every orderable Hetzner GPU server into one table: GPU, VRAM, CPU, RAM, storage, location, net and gross price, setup fee, term and cost per GB of VRAM. It then covers which LLM sizes fit on 24 and 96 GB, what self-managed operation involves and when an API is the better choice. All figures as of 13 October 2026.

...

No longer in the range are the GEX44 with an RTX 4000 SFF Ada (20 GB GDDR6), whose product page redirects to the GEX45 and whose order page lists it as currently not available, and the GEX130 with an RTX 6000 Ada (48 GB). Hetzner does not list data centre GPUs such as the H100 or H200.

...

All prices include one IPv4 address (€1.70 net per month), as of 13 October 2026. Hetzner's English press releases state net prices ("All prices without VAT"), the German ones gross prices with 19% VAT; the website adds VAT depending on the selected country.

| Model | Month net | Month gross (19% VAT) | Setup net | € per GB VRAM per month | € per GB VRAM over 12 months incl. setup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEX45 | €214.00 | €254.66 | €209 | €8.92 | €9.64 |
| GEX63 | €999.00 | €1,188.81 | €999 | €10.41 | €11.27 |
| GEX131-1 | €1,499.00 | €1,783.81 | €1,499 | €15.61 | €16.92 |
| GEX131-2 | €2,099.00 | €2,497.81 | €2,099 | €21.86 | €23.69 |
| GEX131-3 | €2,699.00 | €3,211.81 | €2,699 | €28.11 | €30.46 |

...

Prices are rising. The GEX131 launched in December 2025 at €889 net without a setup fee (since 16 December 2025: €159). In the price list for the 15 June 2026 adjustment, the GEX131-1 was listed at €1,197.30 excluding IPv4 with a €599 setup fee. On 13 October 2026 it is €1,499 and €1,499. The GEX44 cost €184 net at its launch in March 2024.

## Hourly price and billing

Besides the monthly price, Hetzner lists an hourly price. According to the billing documentation, usage is billed by the hour, partial hours are rounded up, and the total never exceeds the monthly price.

| Model | Hourly price net | Monthly price reached after | One week (168 h) incl. setup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEX45 | €0.3429 | 624 hours | €266.61 |
| GEX63 | €1.6009 | 624 hours | €1,267.95 |
| GEX131-1 | €2.4022 | 624 hours | €1,902.57 |
| GEX131-2 | €3.3638 | 624 hours | €2,664.12 |
| GEX131-3 | €4.3253 | 624 hours | €3,425.65 |

For planning this means:

- From about 26 days of runtime, the full monthly price applies.
- Switching off saves nothing. A server is billed as long as it exists in the account. To stop paying, you have to cancel it.
- The setup fee applies per order. For short projects it makes up most of the cost, about 79% of a week on the GEX63.

...

- Data collected: 13 October 2026.
- Hetzner data: product pages and configurator for the GEX45, GEX63 and GEX131, the price data used by the website, press releases and the documentation on GPU servers, provisioning times, billing and price adjustment.

...

Hourly price = server plus IPv4.
- € per GB VRAM per month = net monthly price ÷ VRAM in GB.
- € per GB VRAM over 12 months = (12 × monthly price + setup) ÷ 12 ÷ VRAM.
- Monthly threshold = monthly price ÷ hourly price.
- LLM table: weights = parameters × 2 bytes (FP16), × 1 byte (FP8), × 0.5 bytes (4-bit).

...

- Hetzner: GPU server overview

...

Managed GPU Server 24 with an RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell SFF costs €699 net per month plus €499 setup, Managed GPU Server 96 with an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q costs €2,199 plus €1,999, both cancellable monthly. Included are the dedicated server in a German data centre, one agreed model with vLLM, Open WebUI, 24/7 monitoring, updates with CVE assessment and incident handling according to the service level.
21. ### Does Hetzner offer H100 or H200 GPUs?+

No. In October 2026, Hetzner's GPU range consists of Blackwell-generation RTX PRO cards (RTX PRO 4000 SFF and RTX PRO 6000 Max-Q). Data centre GPUs such as the H100 or H200 are not listed.

results.title: Lambda announces GPU price rises of about 15% — B200, H100 and A100 80GB, from Nov 16 | GPUJournal
highlights:
Nov 6, 2026

Read on Lambda's own pricing page today, Nov 6, 2026: the Instances table now prints the prices that take effect on Nov 16, 2026 — HGX B200 up $1.00 an hour, H100 up $0.60 and A100 80GB up $0.40. It is the largest single announced rise we have caught this autumn, and renters have ten days' notice.

Image: GPUJournal price record — read on lambda.ai/pricing

What was announced, in the pricing page's own words (read Nov 6, 2026): 'These prices take effect November 16, 2026, at 00:00 UTC. Until then, log in to your Lambda Cloud account to see current pricing.' The printed Nov 16 rates: HGX B200 $7.69 an hour (from the $6.69 last verified on Nov 5, +14.9%), HGX H100 $4.59 (from $3.99, +15.0%), HGX A100 80GB $3.19 (from $2.79, +14.3%), and HGX A100 40GB unchanged at $1.99. Lambda is also now at a new address — lambda.com — announced on its blog on Nov 5, 2026; the pricing page itself still answers at lambda.ai/pricing.

How we are treating it: an announced rise is not a live price. Our board keeps Lambda's last verified rates until Nov 16 and will move only when the new rates are re-verified in effect on or after that date — the rise is recorded in Price Watch today as announced, with both dates. One consequence of the announcement is already live, though: Lambda's currently-effective rates can no longer be read on its public page, only after logging in, so today's public check could verify the future rates but not re-read the current ones.

highlights:
The median advertised on-demand price of an H100 GPU-hour was $3.93 in the week of 9 Nov 2026, across 44 providers — up 31% on the same week a year earlier ($2.99). The B200 moved +47% over the same year, to $8.10.

Median of each provider's median advertised on-demand price. Chips with fewer providers move more from week to week.

...

Published rate cards tell a different story from marketplaces. Our price board — built from the on-demand prices cloud providers publish — put the on-demand H100 hour at $4.11 on 13 Nov 2026, against a marketplace median of $3.93 in the week of 9 Nov 2026.

Neither number is “the” price. List prices show what providers ask for capacity on demand; marketplace medians show where spare capacity clears; reserved and contract prices, usually lower again, sit in agreements that are rarely published in full. For anyone valuing a neocloud, lending against GPUs or underwriting a datacentre lease, the spread between the three says how tight capacity is.

results.title: The H100 got more expensive · Three Phase. Potentia Intelligence.
results.author: Jose Mir
highlights:
What happened: Nebius raised on-demand GPU prices on October 1, its second hike in about three months. Independent trackers show the same direction across the market.

Why it matters: The bear case on AI infrastructure assumed GPUs lose value fast. Rental rates are the cleanest test of that assumption, and so far the test is failing.

By the numbers:

- Nebius list price for an H100 went from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU-hour; B300 from $7.85 to $9.50.
- The Ornn H100 index settled at $3.17 on October 23, up about 4% in a month.

results.title: Nebius GPU prices rise across the board, up to… · Slicast
highlights:
# Nebius GPU prices rise across the board, up to 21%; H100 cumulative gain of 53% over five months

Trade press Slicast · October 1, 2026 at 21:01 UTC · Global · Source: KuCoin News

A notable shift is emerging in the AI computing power market: while cloud providers continue to expand their data centers, rental prices for certain high-end GPUs are not declining with increased supply—they continue to rise.

According to a price adjustment notice sent by Nebius to its customers, effective October 1, 2026, the company plans to increase prices for multiple on-demand GPU instances by approximately 17% to 21%. The proposed hourly rates per GPU are: H100 rising from $3.85 to $4.50 (a 16.9% increase), H200 from $4.50 to $5.40 (20% increase), B200 from $7.15 to $8.50 (18.9% increase), and B300 from $7.85 to $9.50 (21% increase).

This price adjustment sends a significant signal: the pace of growth in AI computing demand may still outstrip the rate at which high-end GPUs, power, and data center capacity are coming online. Unlike traditional cloud computing,

...

At the Goldman Sachs Technology Conference, Nebius management stated that the company's visibility into customer demand has extended from approximately 18 months to over 24 months, with some customers already reserving compute capacity for the first half of 2028. The company previously conducted price testing for scarce Blackwell capacity, achieving transaction prices approximately 15% higher than previous peak prices and roughly 20% higher than standard sales pipeline quotes.

...

Nebius signals the opposite: the company is raising prices not only for new B200 and B300 models but also for H100 and H200, which have been on the market for years. This indicates that demand extends beyond the latest architecture, with previous-generation GPUs still offering sufficient performance and cost efficiency for model fine-tuning, inference, scientific computing, and certain enterprise workloads.

...

However, the on-demand price increase will not uniformly raise all of Nebius's revenue by 20%. Large customers typically sign multi-year contracts with fixed prices, minimum purchase volumes, and service terms that cannot be immediately repriced according to new public rates. This adjustment most directly impacts on-demand and short-term compute contracts rather than long-term capacity agreements already signed by clients like Meta.

results.title: Nebius and CoreWeave Lift Nvidia GPU Prices by Up to 21% - Etf Alerts
highlights:
Nvidia rental prices are rising even for last-generation H100s. Nebius has posted an October 1, 2026 on-demand card that lifts selected Nvidia GPU-hour rates by 16.9% to 21.0%. CoreWeave said on September 17 that it is still signing compute at higher prices, including short contracts at about $40 million per megawatt of annualized revenue. A landlord can charge more for a chip it does not make only while that chip stays scarce. That is the signal behind Nvidia, and it is the opposite of a capacity glut.

Nebius’s price page, checked on October 2, still prints two columns. On-demand H100 is $3.85 per GPU-hour. The column marked effective October 1 is $4.50. The same split runs through the H200, the B200, and the B300. Reuters reported on September 17 that this was the second pay-as-you-go increase in about three months, with selected Nvidia GPU rates up 17% to 21%. The card on nebius.com/prices matches that range. It does not show every customer already paying the new rate.

## The card Nebius posted

Four Nvidia rows have a public before and after. GB200 NVL72 and GB300 NVL72 racks are still “contact us” in both columns. RTX PRO 6000 stays at $1.80. L40S “from” rates do not move. The hike lands on the accelerators customers are queued for.

| Nvidia GPU | Prior on-demand column | Announced October 1 card | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| HGX H100 | $3.85 | $4.50 | +$0.65, or 16.9% |
| HGX H200 | $4.50 | $5.40 | +$0.90, or 20.0% |
| HGX B200 | $7.15 | $8.50 | +$1.35, or 18.9% |
| HGX B300 | $7.85 | $9.50 | +$1.65, or 21.0% |

...

Announced Nebius on-demand rates for October 1, 2026, set against the prior on-demand column still printed on the same page. These are posted card rates, not a receipt. The live page and a third-party tracker still disagree, so this chart does not show what every customer is paying. Source: nebius.com/prices, checked October 2, 2026.

...

October 2 is after the effective date, and the page still shows both numbers. The left-hand label is still “On-demand, GPU-hour.” The right-hand label is “GPU-hour (Effective October 1, 2026).” A customer cannot tell, from the page alone, which figure the console will bill.

GPU Finder’s Nebius page, with availability checked at 06:23 UTC on October 2, still listed one-GPU on-demand rates of $3.85 for the H100, $7.15 for the B200, and $7.85 for the B300. Those are the old column. The same check already showed the H200 at $5.40, the new column, with a spot print of $2.45 beside it. The H100 spot print on that row was $2.15. The tracker has not frozen. It has moved one of the four headline GPUs and left the other three on the pre-October number. Treating the whole book as repriced at midnight on October 1 would be tidier, and it would be wrong.

## What moved in 2026

- Prices are rising again for flagships. At least one large specialist cloud announced increases of 10 to 26% on H100, H200 and B300 from December 1.
- Clusters cost more than single instances. Multi-node offers are commonly 20 to 50% more per GPU than on-demand single servers.
- Listed is not available. Several providers list GPUs with no deployable region, or “contact sales” for every flagship.
- Fees moved to storage and idle time. Egress is mostly free; stopped-instance storage, public IPs and minimum billing periods are where extra cost appears.
